column12: fieldDescription

Enables [KMU Map Layers] and all related components (sidebar, mouseover effect, etc.). Map layers are rendered on sector map widgets (map screen, intel screen, Random Assortment of Things minimap replacement, etc.) as an information and presentation tool, with no effect on gameplay. Can be safely toggled on and off on a save. [Default: true].
Enables the [KMU Market Condition Manager] ([MCM]). Currently [UNFINISHED]. [Default: false].

How long the map layers take to fade off the screen when they are hidden (and to fade back in when they are shown again), in seconds. Everything the layers draw fades together - the overlay, its names, and the overlay control box. 0 switches them straight off with no animation; higher makes the fade slower and smoother, up to 2 seconds. [Default: 0.25].
Line width of the outer border framing the political-map overlay control box, in pixels; 0 draws no border. [Default: 1].
Background opacity of the political-map overlay control box, as a percentage: 0 is fully transparent, 100 fully opaque. [Default: 80].

How long the overlay control box takes to fold down to its docked rail (and to unfold again) when you click its collapse handle, in seconds. 0 snaps it instantly with no animation; higher makes the slide slower and smoother, up to 2 seconds. [Default: 0.25].
How far down from the top edge of the screen the political-map overlay control box sits, in pixels - clears the sector map's tab strip so the box does not overlap it. [Default: 36].
How far in from the left edge of the screen the political-map overlay control box sits, in pixels. [Default: 9].

How far above the bottom edge of the screen the political-map overlay control box must stay, in pixels. The box caps its height to this margin so it never runs off the bottom; when the faction/alliance list is longer than the room left, the list scrolls within it while the controls above stay pinned. [Default: 79].

column5: Intel screen map visor top padding
column12: How far down from the top edge of the intel screen's map preview (the visor) the political-map overlay control box sits, in pixels - pushes the box below the vanilla Starscape and fuel-range toggles at the top of that map, leaving the same three-pixel channel those toggles keep between themselves. The box overlays the visor, flush against its left edge, and its height is capped by the visor's bottom. [Default: 21].

column9: UI palette, Chrome grey, Player faction
column12: Which palette the overlay control box is coloured from - its frame, its controls, and its tab row together. UI palette uses the game's own button colours, the same ones every vanilla panel around the box answers to, so the box does not change colour when your faction does. Chrome grey drops the accent hue entirely and draws the box in the plain greys the game writes its text in. Player faction paints it in your faction's own colours, which is what the box did before this setting existed. On an unmodified game UI palette and Player faction look the same; they part once a faction recolours (Nexerelin and modded player factions do). [Default: UI palette].

Which colour the arrow on the overlay control box's collapse handle draws in. Gold picks the standard highlight colour, so the arrow stands out from the box it hangs off. Panel accent draws it in the box's own colours instead - whichever palette the colour scheme above names - brightening when you point at it, so the handle reads as part of the frame. [Default: Gold].
The smallest height (world units) a line of a map label may render at - the readability floor. A cluster too small to hold even one line this tall anywhere shows no name. [Default: 200].
The largest height (world units) a line of a map label may render at, so a roomy cluster does not draw an oversized label. The upper bound of the font-size fit. [Default: 4000].

The most lines a map label may wrap into, on word boundaries. A multi-line block is chosen only when it renders a strictly larger font than the single long line would - wrapping shortens the widest line and spends the cluster's spare girth. 1 forces single-line names. [Default: 3].
The line-height multiple between a multi-line name's stacked lines, so a two- or three-line block is that much taller than the raw line heights. 1 sets the lines flush. [Default: 1.15].

Master switch for everything the map does in answer to the cursor, on every map layer: the hover effects (the halo around the hovered territory and the wash on its cell) and the hover tooltip (the box naming what you are pointing at). Turn off to leave the map unresponsive to hovering - this also skips the per-frame cursor read behind both, so hovering costs nothing while it is off. The two switches below turn off one kind of answer at a time, and each layer has the same pair on its own tab. [Default: true].

Whether the map lights up under the cursor, on every map layer: a halo blooms around the hovered territory and a wash lifts the hovered system's own cell. Turn off to leave the hover tooltip working while nothing is painted over the map. [Ignored while Enable hovering is off]. [Default: true].

Whether the hover tooltip - the small box that appears at the cursor naming the star system under it (and its owner) - shows, on every map layer. Separate from Enable hover effects above (the halo and cell wash); this is the info box. [Ignored while Enable hovering is off]. [Default: true].

How much smaller each step of indent inside a hover tooltip draws than the step above it, in pixels. 0 draws the whole box at one size and leaves the indent alone to say how deep a line sits; 2 steps a four-level breakdown down from 15 to 9, fitting more into the box at the cost of legibility. [Default: 0.75].

The room left under a line of a hover tooltip before the next one, in pixels. Applies wherever the two sliders below do not, so it is the spacing between the box's headings and the things listed directly under them. [Default: 4].

The room left under a line two steps in from the box's own heading, in pixels - where a box states the terms one listed thing's number was summed from. On the political map those are a colony's size, stability and patrols: a long run of lines that a tighter gap packs down without touching the rest of the box. [Default: 0.5].

The room left under a line three steps in, in pixels - where one of those terms breaks down further. On the political map those are the small, medium and large patrols counted behind a colony's patrol term, read as one tally and so tightened hardest. [Default: 0].

How thick the line running from a label across to its value in a hover tooltip is, in pixels. The value column sits at the box's right edge however short the label is, so the line is what carries the eye across the gap between them. 0 draws no lines at all. Below 1 the line no longer covers a whole pixel row, so it strengthens and fades as the box follows the cursor - to make it lighter, use the opacity below instead. [Default: 1].

How strongly that line draws, as a fraction of the tooltip's own opacity. A solid line reads heavier than text of the same shade, because letters spend much of their edge half-transparent where a line does not - so a value below 1 is what sets the line level with the greyed-out text either side of it rather than above it. 0 draws no lines at all. [Default: 0.65].

How much of a line's colour is taken off the blocks a withheld name draws as, where a hover tooltip states that something is there without naming it. A solid block reads heavier than text of the same shade, because letters spend much of their edge half-transparent where a block does not - so a value above 0 is what sets the blocks level with the words either side of them rather than above them. 0 fills them in the line's own colour; 1 fills them black. [Default: 0.4].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color, No color
column12: Which faction palette colour the outer (national) border draws in, or No color to hide it. [Default: Primary faction color].
Political map opacity of the outer (national) border for faction systems. [Default: 1].
Political map line width of the outer (national) border for faction systems, in pixels. [Default: 3].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color, No color
column12: Which faction palette colour the inner (province seam) borders draw in, or No color to hide them. [Default: Primary faction color].
Political map opacity of the inner (province seam) borders for faction systems. [Default: 0.1].
Political map line width of the inner (province seam) borders for faction systems, in pixels. [Default: 10].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color, No color
column12: Which faction palette colour the territory fill draws in, or No color to leave it unfilled. [Default: Primary faction color].
Political map fill opacity for faction systems. [Default: 0.4].

How opaque each faction cluster's name draws, as a fraction of its owner's colour: 1 draws faction names at full strength, lower fades only the faction names so they recede behind the fills and borders. Independent space's names have their own Name opacity. The map's own zoom fade still dims names further at the edges of its zoom range. [Default: 1].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color, No color
column12: Which independent palette colour the outer (national) border draws in, or No color to hide it. [Default: Primary faction color].
Political map opacity of the outer (national) border for independent-held systems. [Default: 0.5].
Political map line width of the outer (national) border for independent-held systems, in pixels. [Default: 3].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color, No color
column12: Which independent palette colour the inner (province seam) borders draw in, or No color to hide them. [Default: Primary faction color].
Political map opacity of the inner (province seam) borders for independent-held systems. [Default: 0.1].
Political map line width of the inner (province seam) borders for independent-held systems, in pixels. [Default: 10].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color, No color
column12: Which independent palette colour the territory fill draws in, or No color to leave it unfilled. [Default: Primary faction color].
Political map fill opacity for independent-held systems. [Default: 0.2].

How opaque each independent-held cluster's name draws, as a fraction of its owner's colour: 1 draws independent names at full strength, lower fades only the independent names so they recede behind the fills and borders. Faction systems have their own Name opacity. The map's own zoom fade still dims names further at the edges of its zoom range. [Default: 1].
Political map outline opacity for decivilised systems - known dead colonies, drawn in the shared neutral colour. 0 hides the outline. [Default: 0.45].
Political map outline line width for decivilised systems, in pixels. [Default: 3].

Political map fill opacity for decivilised systems - the neutral-colour wash inside each dead system's outline, so a dead colony reads as occupied territory rather than a bare ring. 0 leaves it unfilled and draws the outline alone. [Default: 0.15].
Political map outline opacity for uninhabited systems (drawn only while the overlay sidebar's uninhabited-systems checkbox is on). [Default: 0.15].
Political map outline line width for uninhabited systems, in pixels. [Default: 3].

How far a system the spotlit faction lives in but does not claim is washed toward white, as the fraction of the way there: the cell keeps the shared neutral colour and only its brightness lifts, so it reads clear of the sunk greys around it without taking on a faction hue. 0 leaves it at the plain neutral, 1 goes to white. [Default: 1].

How far the Mute non-allied factions toggle (in the Alliances view's on-map sidebar) dims a non-allied faction's borders, fills, and name, as a fraction of its normal opacity: 0.5 halves it, 0 hides it, 1 leaves it unchanged. Alliances are never dimmed. [Ignored while Mute non-allied factions is off]. [Default: 0.5].

How far a Desaturate sidebar toggle sinks a receded bloc's colour toward black, as the fraction of brightness removed: a desaturated bloc paints a uniform grey based on the Independent faction's own colour, darkened by this much so it reads behind genuine independent-held space. Applies wherever Desaturate recedes a bloc - the spotlight filter's faded backdrop (any bloc that is not spotlit, alliances included) and the Alliances view's non-allied factions. 0 leaves it at the Independent colour, 0.5 draws it 50%% darker, 1 goes to black. Desaturate starts on, so this applies from the first spotlight; [it is read only while at least one Desaturate toggle is ticked]. [Default: 0.5].

Whether a system draws a banded stroke inside its own cell border, with a run of colour per colony, saying which factions hold colonies there and how many. Where more than one faction holds colonies, that is the one thing the cell's own colour cannot say - the faction the cell is coloured for is in the band too, so the rivals beside it have a scale to read against. A system only one faction holds colonies in bands too, saying how many are there where its colour has already said whose they are; how loudly it does so is the setting below's business. [Default: true].

Whether each colony in an uncontested system's band draws at a single band width instead of the Colony run length below, so a large holding nobody contests reads as a tally of what is there rather than out-shouting the contested systems beside it. The separator between colonies keeps its own length either way. Systems more than one faction holds colonies in are unaffected - a contest always draws at the Colony run length. [Default: true].

column5: Keep bands clear of cluster names
column12: Whether the bands keep out of the way of the cluster names, each band breaking around the room a name takes over its cell so the words stay readable. Off lets a band run its whole ring, with any name over the cell drawn straight across it - which of the two readouts wins the room they share is a matter of taste, so it is not decided for you. [Default: true].

column5: What a band keeps clear of
column9: The name's fitted box, The words themselves
column12: How much room a cluster name is taken to need, where a band keeps clear of one. The words themselves gives up only the ring each drawn line actually covers. The name's fitted box gives up the whole box the name was placed into, which reaches past the words at both ends - the placement accepts any span at least as long as the name, so the spare is room nothing is ever drawn in. [Ignored while Keep bands clear of cluster names is off]. [Default: The words themselves].

Whether a system that has a band to draw draws one even where its cell leaves no room for it. A cluster name covering the whole of a cell's ring is ignored rather than leaving that cell bare, and a cell too narrow to hold the band and its inset together gives up the inset rather than the band. Off, such a cell simply draws nothing - which is tidier, and leaves no way to tell a system with nothing to say from one that was refused the room to say it. [Default: true].

How thick the presence band is, in world units - the units the map's cells are cut in, so a band keeps the same share of its cell's outline at every zoom. Higher reads from further out; lower keeps it a fine line inside the border. [Default: 200].

How far clear of its cell's own border the presence band runs, in world units, so it reads as sitting inside the border rather than thickening it. Higher pulls the band deeper into the cell; 0 lays it against the border. A cell with no room for the band and this gap together draws none at all. [Default: 200].

How far the run one colony draws in the presence band reaches, measured in band widths. Read against the separator length below: the wider the gap between the two, the more one faction's stretch of band reads as several separate colonies rather than a single large holding. [Default: 3].

How far a darker parting in the presence band reaches, measured in band widths. It parts two colonies of the same faction, and it also closes off a faction's whole stretch where the next faction's begins - drawn in the outgoing faction's own darker shade, so it reads as that faction's holdings ending rather than as a gap belonging to nobody. The last stretch in a band is left open. [Default: 1].

Whether the political map paints its own hover highlight: a halo around the hovered territory and a wash over the hovered system's own cell, both in the hovered territory's colour. Turns the highlight off for this map alone and leaves every other map layer's alone; the Map - Visuals tab's Enable hover effects turns them all off at once. [Ignored while either switch above it is off]. [Default: true].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color
column12: Which palette colour of the territory under the cursor the hover highlight draws in - both the halo around the hovered territory and the wash on the hovered system's own cell. Uninhabited and decivilised cells have no faction palette, so they highlight in the neutral colour. Use Enable hover effects above to switch the whole highlight off. [Default: Secondary faction color].

How bright the halo around the hovered territory burns at its inner edge, as an opacity: the innermost of its stacked strokes draws at this, and the outer ones fade away from it. 0 hides the halo, leaving only the hovered system's own cell wash. [Default: 0.5].

How far the halo blooms off the hovered territory's border, in pixels - the width of its widest, faintest stroke. Higher spreads a softer, wider glow; lower keeps it a tight rim on the border. [Default: 14].

How many strokes the halo is built from, each wider and fainter than the last, so they add up into a soft outward falloff. More layers smooth the falloff at the cost of re-stroking the whole hovered border once more per layer; 1 draws a single flat rim. [Default: 4].

How much of its opacity the halo gives up at the dimmest point of its pulse, as a fraction: 0 holds it perfectly steady, 0.25 lets it breathe down to three quarters brightness and back, 1 fades it out completely each cycle. [Default: 0].
How long one full breath of the halo's pulse takes, in seconds - lower pulses faster. [Ignored while Halo pulse strength is 0]. [Default: 0.2].

How brightly the single star system under the cursor washes over its own coloured cell, as an opacity, so the exact system reads apart from the territory around it. 0 leaves only its outline. [Default: 0.35].

How brightly the hovered system's cell is traced all the way round, as an opacity. Kept separate from the wash because a system deep inside its own faction's territory draws no border of its own - the trace is the only thing that shows where its cell ends. 0 leaves only the wash. [Default: 0.8].
Line width of the trace around the hovered system's cell, in pixels. [Default: 2].

column9: Primary faction color, Secondary faction color
column12: Which palette colour of the faction or alliance you point at in the overlay control box's list the preview lights its systems in - both the wash over the lit cells and the thin trace around them. One colour for the whole set, taken from that faction rather than from each cell it lights, so the preview still reads in its own colour over a map the spotlight filter has faded - and on the brighter of the two shades by default, for the same reason. [Default: Primary faction color].

How brightly each lit system washes over its own coloured cell, as an opacity, so a system the faction merely has a presence in reads as brightly as one it holds outright. 0 leaves only the thin trace around the lit regions. [Default: 0.6].

Whether the political map shows its own hover box - the hovered star system named, with the factions ranked behind the colour it is filled in. Turns the box off for this map alone and leaves every other map layer's alone; the Map - Visuals tab's Enable hover tooltips turns them all off at once. [Ignored while either switch above it is off]. [Default: true].

Whether the territory fills - each cluster's own colour, and the hatch over a contested one - paint below the map's nebulae or above them. Raising the fills raises the borders with them whatever the Borders setting says, because a fill painted over its own borders leaves a blank cell; the hover highlight goes up with them too, since it brightens the fill beneath the cursor. Above paints clear of the haze the Starscape look lays over the sector, Below is dimmed by it. The schematic look has no such haze, so there the setting only reorders the overlay against itself. [Default: Below].

Whether the borders - cluster boundaries, province seams, and the outlines around decivilised and uninhabited systems - paint below the map's nebulae or above them. Borders may be lifted on their own, but they cannot be sunk below the fills: [while Territory fills is set to Above, the borders paint above whatever this says]. Above paints clear of the haze the Starscape look lays over the sector, Below is dimmed by it. The schematic look has no such haze, so there the setting only reorders the overlay against itself. [Default: Below].

Whether the presence bands - the banded stroke inside a cell's border saying which factions hold colonies there - paint below the map's nebulae or above them. Below is dimmed by the haze the Starscape look lays over the sector, Above paints clear of it. The schematic look has no such haze, so there the setting only reorders the overlay against itself. [Default: Below].

Whether the cluster names paint below the map's nebulae or above them. Above paints clear of the haze the Starscape look lays over the sector, Below is dimmed by it - which reaches words rather than shapes, so it is the one of these settings that decides whether a name is read at all rather than how strongly it reads. The schematic look has no such haze, so there the setting only reorders the overlay against itself. [Default: Above].

Master switch for stability scaling. When on, each dominance factor (colony size, station bonus, patrols) is cut at low stability by its own low-stability penalty below, so a destabilised colony holds less of its system than a functioning one. Turn off to ignore stability entirely and rank colonies by their raw weighted size, station, and patrol sum. [Default: true].

Multiply how much each colony's raw size weighs on its system's dominant faction, before stability scales it and the station and patrol bonuses are added. A hidden market uses this on whichever size the Hidden markets section selects. 1 counts size as-is; below 1 flattens the gap between large and small colonies, above 1 widens it; 0 drops raw size entirely (a colony then holds a system only through its station or patrol bonus, if any). [Default: 1].

How much a colony's own size weight is cut when its stability is at zero, as a fraction: 1 removes it entirely at zero stability (half at 5, full at 10), 0.5 leaves it half its weight at zero stability, 0 ignores stability for colony size. [Applies only while Stability weighs dominance is on]. [Default: 1].

How a hidden market (a secret colony such as a pirate base or the Galatia Academy) counts toward its system's dominant faction. Normal weighs it by its real colony size like any colony; Fixed folds it in at the Hidden market fixed weight below, regardless of size, so a large secret base never outweighs the open colonies around it. Both then take the colony size weight and stability. [Default: Fixed].

The fixed size rating a hidden market folds in at while Hidden market scaling is Fixed, in place of its real size, before the colony size weight and stability apply. 1 counts a hidden market as a single size point; higher lets a secret base mark more presence. [Ignored while Hidden market scaling is Normal]. [Default: 1].

Give a colony with an attached defensive station extra size points toward its system's dominant faction (see Station weight), so a stationed colony outranks an otherwise-identical unstationed one. A hidden market's station earns a fraction of it (see Hidden-market station fraction), and how much the bonus survives low stability is set by the Station low-stability penalty. Turn off to rank colonies without any station bonus. [Default: true].

How many size points an attached defensive station adds to a visible colony's dominance contribution, before its low-stability penalty applies. 1 makes a station worth a single colony size point; below 1 softens the bonus, above 1 sharpens it; 0 removes it. A hidden market earns this scaled by the Hidden-market station fraction. [Ignored while Station weighs dominance is off]. [Default: 1].

The fraction of the Station weight a station on a hidden market earns, so a fortified secret base reads above a bare unstationed hidden market without matching an openly held stationed colony. 0 gives hidden markets no station bonus; 1 gives them the full station weight. [Ignored while Station weighs dominance is off]. [Default: 0.5].

How much the station bonus is cut when the colony's stability is at zero, as a fraction: 1 removes it entirely at zero stability, 0.5 leaves it half at zero stability, 0 keeps the full station bonus regardless of stability. [Applies only while Stability weighs dominance is on]. [Default: 0.5].

Give a colony extra size points toward its system's dominant faction for the patrols its military bases field, weighted by patrol size (see the three patrol weights below). Reads the colony's configured patrol strength from the economy, so it counts steadily rather than tracking the fleets currently in flight. [Default: true].

How many size points each small (light) patrol a colony fields adds toward its system's dominant faction, before the patrol low-stability penalty applies. [Ignored while Patrols weigh dominance is off]. [Default: 0.3].

How many size points each medium patrol a colony fields adds toward its system's dominant faction, before the patrol low-stability penalty applies. [Ignored while Patrols weigh dominance is off]. [Default: 0.6].

How many size points each large (heavy) patrol a colony fields adds toward its system's dominant faction, before the patrol low-stability penalty applies. [Ignored while Patrols weigh dominance is off]. [Default: 1.2].

How much a colony's patrol bonus is cut when its stability is at zero, as a fraction: 1 removes it entirely at zero stability, 0.5 leaves it half at zero stability, 0 keeps the full patrol bonus regardless of stability. [Applies only while Stability weighs dominance is on]. [Default: 0.5].

How loudly the overlay control box's own furniture sounds as the cursor reaches it - a tab in its header, or its collapse handle. 1 is the game's own mouseover level, the one every vanilla button plays at; below that the box answers more quietly than the chrome around it, and 0 silences that one kind of thing. With this and the two below all at 0 the box makes no sound under the cursor at all. [Default: 0.5].
How loudly a control with one answer to give - a tick box, a switch - sounds as the cursor reaches it. Same scale as above: 1 is the game's own mouseover level and 0 is silence. [Default: 0.5].

How loudly one of many alike - one option of a row of them, one row of a list - sounds as the cursor reaches it. Set below the two above because a cursor crossing the box sweeps several of these on the way to the one thing you aimed at; raised to match them, a column of listed items is what makes the box chatter. 0 is silence. [Default: 0.25].

How loudly the overlay control box's list sounds as the wheel scrolls it. One sound for the whole movement rather than one per row that passes under a parked cursor - you turned the wheel once. 0 is silence. [Default: 0.5].

How loudly the map ticks as the cursor reaches a new star system's cell - the same moment the hover tooltip changes what it is naming. Silenced by 0 here, and by the hovering switches on the Map - Visuals tab along with everything else the map does in answer to the cursor. [Default: 0.5].

column8: Rebind any shortcut on this tab by clicking its button and pressing a key. Press [Escape] while rebinding to leave it unbound.

column12: Keyboard shortcut that ticks and unticks the [Map layers] box on the map's own filter row, showing and hiding everything the overlay draws. Live only on map and intel screens. [Default: M].
Keyboard shortcut that jumps the political-map overlay's layer bar to the No Layer view, painting nothing. [Default: N].
Keyboard shortcut that jumps the political-map overlay's layer bar to the Factions view, painting faction territory. [Default: P].
Show [market entities marked as discoverable] the player has not gotten close to yet. [Default: false].
Show [markets marked as hidden] before the player has seen them where they stand or their system is settled by any faction (e.g. Galatia Academy in Galatia). [Default: false].

column5: Show decivilised worlds surveyed at least to
column12: Survey level required for [decivilised colonies] to be revealed. [Default: Seen].
Show [unowned (neutral) markets with Abandoned Station condition] before the player has seen them where they stand or their system is settled by any faction. [Default: false].

Seed map geometry for [every star system in the sector], not just the reachable, visible, or inhabited ones - forces a cell onto a system the map would otherwise omit. A forced system draws as uninhabited unless it holds a colony. [Default: false].

column5: Constrain layers to their own map
column12: Constrain the current M-map map layer to render on the M-map only, and the intel screen map layer on the intel screen. Prevents map layers rendering in modded UI, e.g. the minimap from Random Assortment of Things. The hook the layers draw through belongs to the sector map by convention only, and any mod that builds a map of its own drives it too - which is why layers show up in one. Leave off to keep seeing them there; turn on if a modded map draws them wrongly, or if you would rather they appeared only on the vanilla screens. [Default: false].

column5: Allow hovering on every map surface
column12: Let map layer mouseover effects and tooltips answer the cursor anywhere, including maps built by other mods on any screen. Off, they answer on the M-map and the intel screen only. A modded map draws at its own position and zoom, and the cursor read cannot tell that transform from the vanilla one - so pointing anywhere on screen resolves a star system through it, lighting cells and sounding the mouseover tick with no map open. In hyperspace that is every cursor movement, since hyperspace and sector map coordinates are the same space. Turn on only if you want a modded map to answer the cursor and accept that the answer may name the wrong system. [Default: false].

column5: Allow hovering while no screen is open
column12: Also let map layer mouseover effects and tooltips answer the cursor while you are looking at the campaign itself - no map, intel or other screen open, and no conversation up. That is where a mod that docks a map where the campaign radar was, such as Random Assortment of Things, puts the only map on screen. Narrower than the switch above, which permits every surface on every screen; with that one on, this adds nothing. Costs nothing on an install without such a map, there being no map drawn on the campaign view to hover in the first place. Turn off if a modded map you can see on the campaign view should stay quiet. [Has no effect if Constrain layers to their own map is on], since no layer is drawn there to hover. [Default: true].

column5: Random Assortment of Things compatibility mode
column12: Treat the minimap from Random Assortment of Things as a map worth answering, rather than as one more surface to stand clear of. That minimap takes the campaign radar's place and is on screen with no map screen open, so it is the one modded map the player is deliberately pointing at. [Engages only when that mod is installed and its own Enable Mini-map setting is on], so an install without the minimap behaves the same either way. It works inside the two constraints above rather than around them: whatever they forbid stays forbidden. It also stops that minimap drawing while the mod has it slid off screen, and lets it draw again the moment any part of it slides back into view: a minimap you cannot see still renders a whole sector map behind whatever screen you opened, which costs the work and can pull the mouseover on the real map away from the pointer. Turn off if the layers misbehave on that minimap, or if you would rather nothing here touched it. [Default: true].

column5: Add map layers toggle to the filter row
column12: Whether the map layers get a tick box of their own in the vanilla filter row - the row the sector map's Starscape, Fuel range and Names toggles sit in, and the shorter band at the top of the intel screen's map. On adds the box to both rows wherever there is room left for it, and it is what shows and hides everything the map layers draw on that screen. Off leaves both rows exactly as the game builds them; with no box on either screen to switch the layers off, they stay shown. This says nothing about whether the map layers are installed - that is the Features tab's switch. [Default: true].

How far each system's coloured territory extends into empty space, in world units, before its frontier edge closes it off. Higher lets each system claim more open space - distant systems' territories grow until they meet and merge; lower pulls every territory in tight around its own systems. [Default: 4000].

Sides of the polygon that rounds each system cell's outer frontier - its reach into empty space. Higher is smoother but adds a vertex per segment to every frontier cell, which can cost map FPS; lower trades a faceted frontier for fewer vertices. [Default: 48].

How far apart two outline points may be and still merge into one corner when chaining the border, in world units. Raise if faction borders go missing; too high merges distinct corners. Always applied - this is the raw ring tracing, upstream of the spike and rounding passes below. [Default: 100].

A corner whose inset point would jut past this multiple of the border inset is bevelled flat instead of pointed. Lower bevels sharp corners sooner (no inward spikes/loops); higher keeps crisper points. Always applied - part of the inset that traces the ring, not a gated smoothing pass. [Default: 4].

Master switch for the spike-sanding pass in this section, which runs before corner rounding and splices out needle and cusp protrusions the rounding cannot fix. On uses the height and angle below; off skips the pass and leaves those two knobs unread, keeping their values for when you switch it back on. [Default: false].

A sharp corner rising less than this (world units) above its neighbours is a needle or cusp too thin for rounding to fix, so it is sanded off before rounding; a sharp corner that juts farther is kept as real shape. [Ignored while Sand border spikes is off]. [Default: 150].

Only corners sharper than this interior angle (degrees) are candidates for spike sanding; gentler corners and smooth arc facets are kept. Pairs with spike height - a corner must be both sharp and shallow to be sanded. [Ignored while Sand border spikes is off]. [Default: 60].

Master switch for the corner-rounding pass in this section. On replaces each sharp border corner with an arc using the radius, segments, and chamfer below; off leaves the resolved envelope sharp-cornered and leaves those three knobs unread, keeping their values for when you switch it back on. Also gates the factionless (decivilised and uninhabited) cell outlines, so the whole map's corners round or not together. [Default: true].
Corner-rounding radius of the national border, in world units. Higher rounds the cluster outline more; the cut self-limits on short edges. [Ignored while Round border corners is off]. [Default: 300].
Arc segments per rounded corner of the national border. Higher is smoother but adds vertices. [Ignored while Round border corners is off]. [Default: 3].
Corners sharper than this interior angle (degrees) are cut flat (chamfered) instead of given a full arc. [Ignored while Round border corners is off]. [Default: 35].

Corners flatter than this interior angle (degrees) keep their vertex instead of being rounded. A border is cell arcs sampled at fixed angles joined by straight runs, and those samples meet at about 173 degrees, so a setting past them rounds the samples too - roughly twice the border vertices for a line that moves about ten world units. Lower rounds fewer corners and leaves gentle bends sharp. [Ignored while Round border corners is off]. [Default: 170].

Line width of the contested-cluster hatch lines, in pixels. Higher makes the hatch read heavier and darker without changing the line spacing or the solid fill. Only the filter's contested territory hatches. [Default: 50].

Antialiases the contested-cluster hatch instead of stroking it hard-edged. On softens each line's edges, which reads smoother at a wide stroke but also makes the hatch slightly wider, lighter and less crisp against the solid fill beside it, and costs a blend for every pixel the hatch covers. The hatch is the one pass that chooses this for itself - the cluster fills and borders are unaffected either way. [Some GL bridges (Fast Rendering) may ignore the smoothing hint above a one-pixel stroke, in which case this changes nothing on screen]. [Default: false].

The direction the contested-cluster hatch lines run, in degrees off horizontal (a hatch line is undirected, so 0 and 180 match). 0 lays the lines flat, 90 stands them upright, 45 is a diagonal. Only the filter's contested territory hatches. [Default: 45].

The perpendicular gap between the diagonal hatch lines that fill a contested cluster - the spotlighted bloc's present-but-dominated systems under the faction/alliance filter - in world units. Lower packs the hatch denser, higher opens it up. Only the filter's contested territory hatches; every other territory fills solid. [Default: 1000].

How far apart two of one hatch line's crossings may sit and still merge into a single stroke, as a percentage of the hatch spacing (0.2 is a fifth of a percent). A line crossing several of the cluster's triangles is clipped once per triangle, and merging those crossings is what stops a wide line restarting its stair-step phase mid-stroke, which shows as sideways steps and darker ticks. Two triangles sharing an edge should cross a line at the same point exactly; this absorbs a tessellation that does not quite agree. 0 merges only exact abutments, which leaves some of those artefacts visible. [Default: 0.2].

How many directions the label-anchor search fans over the half-circle (0-180 degrees; a label line is undirected). More directions let the accepted line align more closely with the cluster's open space, at a higher search cost. Pure horizontal, the cluster's own principal axis, and the preferred slant are always searched on top of the fan. [Default: 8].

How many parallel lines the search sweeps across the cluster per direction, spaced evenly over the cluster's extent perpendicular to that direction. This is what lets the accepted line slide off the centroid into a roomier part of the cluster - an icon on the centre line relocates the label instead of shrinking it. 1 degenerates to a single centred line per direction. [Default: 10].

How close the search has to land to the largest font height each candidate line holds, in world units. The fit grows the font by halving the size clamp, and every halving re-measures the label's band against the national border and the system icons - the single biggest cost in the map's rebuild - so a coarser tolerance buys those measurements back one for one. 1 is already finer than a map pixel resolves at any zoom; raise it to trade label sizing precision for a faster rebuild, lower it only to see whether the fit was ever precision-limited. [Default: 1].

How much length a shallower (more horizontal) candidate line may give up and still win the search. Each candidate's clear length is scaled by 1 - strength * sin(angle)^exponent, where angle is the line's slope from horizontal. 0 picks the pure longest line regardless of slope; 1 scores a vertical line zero. [Default: 0.3].

How sharply the vertical penalty concentrates toward the perpendicular - the exponent on the line's deviation from the cluster's preferred lean in the score. A higher exponent leaves near-lean lines almost unpenalised and bites only as a line swings far off it. [Default: 2].

How far a label may lean off level to follow its cluster's long axis, in degrees. The anchor search prefers this cluster-specific slant over screen-horizontal, capped here so a tall cluster never stands its name vertical and scaled down toward 0 as a cluster gets rounder (a near-round or tightly clumped cluster has no trustworthy long axis, so it stays level). 0 forces dead-horizontal labels; 90 lets a label follow its axis all the way to vertical. [Default: 45].

How far short of the national border each end of a label anchor stops, in multiples of the border inset channel - the gap a faction name needs so it does not touch the border. A clear line shorter than twice this collapses to the dot. [Default: 4].

The keep-out radius around each system icon that a label anchor must not cross, in world units - an approximation of the icon's on-map footprint, since icons draw at a fixed pixel size. An icon on a cluster's axis shortens the anchor to the clear side rather than letting a name run across the star. [Default: 100].

The fill opacity of the debug band quad - the box the fitted label occupies, drawn over the anchor line. Kept low so the national border reads through the band and an overflow is visible; the whole point of the band is to see it kiss or clear the border. [Default: 0.35].

The opacity of the debug band box's strokes - its outline, the line-count divider rules, the centreline, and the anchor dot. Kept separate from the fill so the outline can read stronger than the faint band wash it sits on. [Default: 0.9].

Draw a dot at each system cluster's centre and, in green, the fitted label line - the cluster's long axis refit to stay inside the national border, clear of system icons, and short of the border by the anchor end inset, leaning horizontal per the anchor bias. The anchor a faction name hangs on; a diagnostic for the label placement behind the faction names. Master switch for the anchor overlay - the two axis toggles below only add lines while this is on. [Default: false].

When a cluster's fitted label line collapses to the dot, also draw in red the best candidate line the fit found before the border, icon, or end-margin trim discarded it - so a near miss can be told from a hopeless cluster while tuning the anchor knobs. Layered under the yellow and green lines. [Only meaningful while Show cluster label anchors is on]. [Default: false].

Also draw in yellow the label line each cluster's fit would accept with no horizontal bias applied, so the anchor bias knob's effect is visible by contrast. Skipped when the unbiased direction matches the accepted line (bias at 1, or an axis already horizontal) - the green line already is the unbiased one. Layered under the green line. [Only meaningful while Show cluster label anchors is on]. [Default: false].

Draw the ring each cell's presence band would run along, with a dot where a band starts (the cell's top centre, running clockwise). Coloured by what the cell's own room allows: green where the authored inset held, yellow where the pad had to be given up to fit a band at all, and red where no band is laid - the pad would have had to go and Always draw a planned band is off, or the cell is narrower than the band is wide. A cell drawing no band looks the same whether nothing is present in it or its ring refused the room, and this is what tells those apart. Draws over the bands themselves so a band can be read against the path it was laid on. [Shows nothing while Presence bands are off]. [Default: false].

Replace the normal political-map render with a border-tracing diagnostic that layers the smoothing pipeline's stages so you can see what each pass did. From bottom to top: the base traced border in red, the despiked border in yellow, and the rounded border in green. Respects the two smoothing gates - a stage draws only when its pass ran, so with sanding off there is no yellow and with rounding off no green. [Default: false].

How hard the sector-map sidebar tab labels read. Same trade as the intel knob beside it - the condensed atlas those tabs are lettered in carries no antialiasing of its own, so interpolated it reads dimmer than the colour it was set in and unfiltered it reads harder than the vanilla tabs directly above it. Settled against those tabs at none at all: the softer end is what matches them, where the intel row beside vanilla's buttons wants nearly all of it. 0 leaves them as the loader hands them over, 1 draws them unfiltered. [Default: 0].

How hard the intel-screen sidebar's raised-button labels read. The atlas those labels are drawn from is a pixel face, and the font loader hands it over interpolated, which costs every single-pixel stroke part of itself and leaves the text reading dimmer than the colour it was set in; drawn unfiltered instead they read harder-edged than the vanilla chrome beside them. 0 leaves them as the loader hands them over, 1 draws them unfiltered, and anything between lays the two over one another at that weight. The default is mostly hard: what matches the vanilla row is the tone rather than the edge. [Default: 0.8].

column9: OFF, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, ALL
column12: Verbosity of KMU's own output in starsector.log. WARN is the normal level; INFO adds routine lines and DEBUG adds per-frame overlay diagnostics. [Default: WARN].

List every market condition in the KMU condition picker, including non-planetary ones the game does not normally offer for hand placement (such as decivilisation). Turn off to restrict the picker to the planetary conditions vanilla treats as hand-placeable. [Default: true].
